comments.author: @CanadaUnchartedTV
comments.text: Interesting video! A strange side of this story: dig deep enough in some fields near Ottawa and you can hit whale bones, belugas, hundreds of kilometres from any ocean. They're only about 11–13 thousand years old, from the Champlain Sea that flooded the land the ice sheet had pressed below sea level. That sea also left a weak marine clay that can suddenly turn to liquid, and in 1971 a landslide in it swallowed part of Saint-Jean-Vianney in Quebec, killing 31 people.
